# Ānisaṁsadassāvīkathā (Kv 9.1)

**ID:** Kv 9.1
**Section:** Kathāvatthu (kv)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Ānisaṁsadassāvīkathā
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m3.mul16.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ānisaṁsadassāvīkathā* ("Debate on One Who Sees the Advantage") is the first discourse in the ninth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, belonging to the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The debate addresses the thesis that for one who contemplates or perceives the advantage (*ānisaṁsadassāvī*), there is abandoning (*pahāna*) of mental fetters [Bareau 1955]. This view, attributed to the Andhaka school, appeals to sutta teachings—specifically connected with the *Nibbānasutta* (AN 7.19)—concerning one who abides observing happiness in Extinction [Bareau 1955]. The orthodox Theravādin position rejects this assertion, contending that abandoning does not occur merely through discerning advantages; rather, defilements are abandoned only by applying attention to the impermanence (*anicca*), suffering (*dukkha*), disease, vanity, and nonself (*anatta*) of conditioned formations (*saṅkhārā*) [Bareau 1955].
